title: Per-job temp scratch is never deleted — no runner finally, no launch sweeper (docs claim both exist)
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/jobs/export-runner.ts:175-186, src/main/index.ts:293-327`

**Problem:** CLAUDE.md and paths.ts:263 both state the per-job scratch dir `<temp>/openclip/<projectId>/<jobId>/` is 'deleted in a finally' and that a 'launch-time temp sweeper reclaims' it. Neither is implemented. No runner has any cleanup finally: the export runner writes a `.ass` into jobTempDir (export-runner.ts:183 via writeClipCaptions → mkdirSync) and never removes it; the transcribe runner writes `<base>.json` next to the WAV (transcribe-runner.ts:118) and never removes it; the url-download runner mkdirs `<temp>/openclip/downloads/<jobId>/` (url-download-runner.ts:32) and never removes it. Result: every transcribe leaves a JSON, every captioned export leaves an .ass, every URL import leaves a full downloaded mp4 in temp, and every import leaves a WAV — unbounded disk growth until OS temp cleanup (which is not guaranteed and not prompt).

**Recommendation:** Either (a) wrap each runner's body in try/finally that rm()s its jobTempDir (the export/transcribe/url-download runners already know projectId+jobId or can derive the dir), AND/OR (b) add a launch-time sweep mirroring sweepOrphanMediaAtLaunch that rm -rf's `<temp>/openclip/<projectId>/<jobId>` dirs not belonging to an active job (sidecar.activeJobIds() at sidecar-manager.ts:225 exists precisely for this and is currently unused). title: Clip/transcript/export edits are never autosaved (lost on quit) — autosave only watches currentProject
description:
**Location:** `src/renderer/src/stores/projectStore/autosave.ts:48-53`

**Problem:** startAutosave subscribes only to `currentProject !== prev.currentProject`. But the real editing actions write to sibling slices, not currentProject: clipsSlice.approveClip/rejectClip/updateClip/setClips, timelineSlice trim (via updateClip), transcriptSlice.hydrate/append, and exportSlice.addExportRecord/markExported. None of these mutate currentProject, so the subscriber never fires for them. There is no quit/blur/visibilitychange save hook either (confirmed: no such listener in src/renderer). The only place live slice state is persisted is the import-controller's re-import flush via composeProject() (import-controller.ts:197), which fires only right before a NEW import. Net effect: a user who imports, approves clips, trims, and quits loses every clip edit/approval/trim and the export history — directly violating PRD P5 done-when ('quit/reopen restores the full project — source, transcript, clips, edits, settings'). The autosave-subscriber.spec even encodes this as intended ('does not save when an unrelated slice changes'), using transcriptSearch as the example — but clip edits are the same kind of 'unrelated slice change' and are NOT transient.

**Recommendation:** Make autosave observe the slices that constitute the saved document. Either (a) subscribe to clips/transcript/exportHistory/settings as well and debounce a composeProject() save, or (b) have the editing actions also bump currentProject (e.g. updatedAt) so the existing subscriber fires, or (c) add a flush-save on app teardown/visibilitychange. Whichever path, the autosave payload must be composeProject() (live slices), not the raw currentProject — see the related save() finding.

title: Burn never line-wraps (WrapStyle:2 + no \N) — long caption lines clip off-frame
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/ass-captions.ts:421`

**Problem:** The script header sets 'WrapStyle: 2', which in ASS means NO automatic word-wrapping — lines break ONLY at an explicit \N. buildKaraokeLine/buildAss never insert a \N inside a Dialogue line; a line is just up to maxWordsPerLine words (default 7) of '{\k..}word' cues. With the wide presets (e.g. MrBeast fontSize 84, Anton/Archivo Black, MarginL/R only 60 on a 1080 canvas), a 7-word line easily exceeds the usable width, and because libass won't wrap it, the text runs off both sides of the 1080px frame and is clipped. The DOM preview, by contrast, uses whiteSpace:'pre-wrap' (caption-css.ts:53) and DOES wrap — so the preview looks fine while the burned clip has captions bleeding off-screen. This is both a clipping bug and a preview/burn divergence.

**Recommendation:** Either switch to 'WrapStyle: 0' (smart wrap, which respects MarginL/R) so libass wraps long lines, or keep WrapStyle:2 but compute and insert explicit \N breaks based on an estimated text width for the chosen font/size. WrapStyle:0 is the lower-risk fix; re-capture the golden .ass strings after the change.

title: Privileged openclip-media:// protocol serves any absolute path on disk (arbitrary file read)
description:
**Location:** `src/main/utils/media-protocol.ts:106-122`

**Problem:** installMediaProtocolHandler decodes req.url to an absolute path via pathFromMediaUrl and net.fetch's pathToFileURL(absPath) with NO restriction to known media directories. The scheme is registered as standard+secure+stream+bypassCSP and is reachable from the renderer (the <video> src is built from Project.sourceVideo.path). The file header CLAIMS 'Nothing here grants the renderer broader filesystem reach than the path it was already handed', but that is false: the handler will serve ANY path the URL encodes. I verified that openclip-media://file/etc/passwd, .../Users/me/.ssh/id_rsa, and .../secrets.json all decode to those exact paths and resolve to file:///etc/passwd etc. A compromised renderer (XSS via transcript/title text rendered in the UI, a malicious dependency, or a tampered .ocproj whose sourceVideo.path points at a secret) can fetch arbitrary local files. Because the scheme has supportFetchAPI:true and a real secure origin, the renderer can read the bytes via fetch() and, under the production CSP (connect-src 'self' https:), POST them to any https endpoint — a full local-file exfiltration chain. There is no traversal even needed; absolute paths are accepted directly.

**Recommendation:** Constrain the handler to an allow-list of roots the app legitimately serves video from: userData/media, the OS temp openclip root, and the set of currently-open projects' sourceVideo paths (or, simplest and tightest, only paths under userData/media plus a per-session registered set of imported originals). After decoding, resolve the real path and assert it startsWith one of those roots (using path.resolve + a trailing-separator check, and ideally fs.realpath to defeat symlink escapes) before net.fetch; otherwise return 403. Reject any path containing NUL or '..' segments defensively.

title: useProject.save() persists stale currentProject.clips/.transcript, discarding live slice edits
description:
**Location:** `src/renderer/src/hooks/useProject.ts:147-154`

**Problem:** projectActions.save() does `const current = store.getState().currentProject; await bridge.project.save({ project: current })`. It saves the raw currentProject, not composeProject(). Since clips/transcript live in their own slices (the source of truth — see exportSlice/import-controller comments), currentProject.clips and currentProject.transcript are the stale snapshot the project was loaded with. So even an EXPLICIT save would write empty/old clips and discard the user's approvals/trims/AI results. The import-controller went out of its way to use composeProject() for exactly this reason (import-controller.ts:48-52, 197), but useProject.save() did not get the same treatment.

**Recommendation:** Route save() through composeProject() (or the same layering composeLiveProject applies) so it persists the live clips + transcript over the base document, mirroring the import-controller flush. Add a unit test asserting that save() after approveClip persists the approved status.

title: Clip approvals, trims, and live transcript are never autosaved or saved (stale currentProject persisted)
description:
**Location:** `src/renderer/src/stores/projectStore/autosave.ts:48-53`

**Problem:** startAutosave subscribes only to `currentProject` reference changes. Clip edits (approveClip/rejectClip/markExported in clipsSlice.ts:65-73), timeline trims (timelineSlice writes `clips`), and streamed transcript edits (transcriptSlice) all call `set({ clips })` / `set({ transcript })` and never mutate `currentProject`, so autosave never fires for them. Worse, when it does fire (e.g. setProjectSettings touches currentProject), installAutosave saves the RAW `currentProject` (autosave.ts:69), not composeProject(), so stale/empty clips are written. The manual save path has the same defect: projectActions.save() persists `store.getState().currentProject` directly (useProject.ts:148-150). The store deliberately keeps clips/transcript as the source of truth and merges them only via composeProject() at export/flush time — meaning the user's approvals and trims are silently lost on quit/reopen, breaking the PRD §5 'quit/reopen restores edits' promise.

**Recommendation:** Persist the composed project, not the raw one: have installAutosave/save call composeProject() before bridge.project.save(), and broaden the autosave trigger so it also fires on clips/transcript slice changes (e.g. subscribe to a derived signature, or have the slice setters bump currentProject.updatedAt). Add a test that approving a clip then advancing the debounce saves a project whose clips include the approval.

title: Bundled FFmpeg is --enable-nonfree, making it legally non-redistributable in the MIT dmg
description:
**Location:** `package.json:38-39 (ffmpeg-static / ffmpeg-ffprobe-static); electron-builder.yml:42-53`

**Problem:** The actual binaries shipped by ffmpeg-static@5.3.0 and ffmpeg-ffprobe-static@6.1.1 are configured with `--enable-gpl --enable-nonfree --enable-version3` (verified by running the installed binaries: ffmpeg reports `--enable-nonfree`, ffprobe reports `--enable-nonfree`). FFmpeg's own docs state that `--enable-nonfree` produces a binary that is *unredistributable* — it may be built for personal use but may NOT be redistributed. OpenClip ships both binaries as extraResources inside a public, MIT-licensed, (intended-to-be) notarized dmg via `publish: generic`. This is a direct license-compliance violation; additionally combining `--enable-gpl` with the app means the GPL'd ffmpeg/ffprobe travel with the product (separate-process invocation usually keeps the app itself out of GPL scope, but the nonfree flag is the hard blocker). The bundle-binaries verifier checks for the libass `subtitles` filter and `h264_videotoolbox` but never inspects the license configuration, so this slips through every build.

**Recommendation:** Switch to LGPL/GPL-clean, non-nonfree static FFmpeg builds (e.g. the BtbN ffmpeg-builds 'gpl' or 'lgpl' variants, or self-build with the same flags minus `--enable-nonfree` and minus the nonfree-only libs like libfdk/openssl-nonfree) and SHA-pin them the way yt-dlp already is. As a guardrail, add an assertion to scripts/bundle-binaries.mjs that runs `ffmpeg -version` and FAILS the build if the configuration line contains `--enable-nonfree`. Re-confirm the redistribution terms before any public release.

title: Autosave swallows save rejections — silent data loss + unhandled promise rejection
description:
**Location:** `src/shared/autosave.ts:59`

**Problem:** The debounced autosave fires via `timer = setTimeout(() => void fire(), delayMs)`. `fire()` calls `await save(snapshot)`, and `save` is the real bridge call `window.openclip.project.save(...)` (autosave.ts installAutosave:69 / useImportController:67-69), which rejects on any IO failure (project-store.ts:104-106 throws ProjectStoreError on a failed writeFile — disk full, permission denied, path gone). Because the timer callback does `void fire()`, that rejection is discarded: the user's edits silently fail to persist AND it becomes an unhandled promise rejection (there is no process-level unhandledRejection handler in main, and on the renderer it just logs to console). The user believes their work is saved when it is not.

**Recommendation:** Catch the rejection from fire() inside the timer and surface it: at minimum route it to a caller-supplied onError so the UI can show a 'save failed' indicator, and avoid the unhandled rejection. The flush() path (line 67, awaited by installAutosave's teardown) has the same issue and should also propagate or report the error rather than letting teardown reject.

title: ffmpeg-static / ffprobe binaries have no SHA verification — a swapped binary slips through
description:
**Location:** `scripts/bundle-binaries.mjs:82-94,383-384`

**Problem:** yt-dlp is pinned and SHA-256-verified against the release SHA2-256SUMS (resolveYtDlp, lines 124-169), and the ONNX wasm/model are staged from node_modules. But the two ffmpeg binaries are taken verbatim from `require('ffmpeg-static')` / `ffmpeg-ffprobe-static.ffprobePath` with zero integrity check. ffmpeg-static downloads its binary on `node install.js` from a GitHub release into a global env-paths cache; neither that package nor this repo records a checksum (confirmed: no createHash/checksum logic in ffmpeg-static or ffmpeg-ffprobe-static install scripts). So the largest, most security-sensitive sidecar — the one that processes untrusted downloaded video — is the ONLY bundled binary that can be silently swapped (poisoned npm cache, MITM of the GitHub download, or a tampered global cache) and then get notarized and shipped without the build noticing. This directly contradicts the stated 'pinned + SHA-verified' posture for the binary supply chain.

**Recommendation:** Pin the expected SHA-256 of the ffmpeg and ffprobe binaries for each supported plat-arch and verify them in installBinary() (or a dedicated step) exactly as resolveYtDlp() does — fail loudly on mismatch. The hashes can be captured once and committed; bumping the package then forces an intentional hash update.

title: splitMotionSeries assumes ffmpeg emits full-left-then-full-right metadata; real ffmpeg likely interleaves the two ROI sinks frame-by-frame
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/reframe-detect.ts:436-449 (and the assumption documented at :428-435, :261-294)`

**Problem:** The 2-speaker motion pass uses a single -filter_complex with two metadata=print chains routed to two -f null sinks ([lm] then [rm]). splitMotionSeries splits the flat parsed {times,values} at its midpoint, assigning values[0..half-1] to `left` and values[half..] to `right`, explicitly relying (comment at :430) on ffmpeg emitting 'the FULL left series followed by the FULL right series'. But with one input decode feeding two filtered outputs, ffmpeg's transcode loop pushes each decoded frame through BOTH chains in lockstep, so the metadata=print log lines interleave per frame (L0,R0,L1,R1,...), not block-sequentially (L0,L1,...,R0,R1,...). Under interleaving, splitMotionSeries assigns the first half of the interleaved stream entirely to `left` and the second half to `right` — completely scrambling which energy belongs to which side and at what time. buildActiveSpeakerSegments then picks the wrong active speaker, and the pan follows the wrong face. The unit test (reframe-detect.spec.ts:277-328) hand-builds a block-sequential fixture, so it cannot catch this; the @serial smoke (reframe.serial.spec.ts) never runs the motion pass at all; and planReframe swallows nothing here (the bug produces a plausible-but-wrong pan, not an exception), so it silently mis-crops.

**Recommendation:** Do not rely on emission order. Disambiguate the two series by filter instance: each metadata=print is a distinct `Parsed_metadata_<N>` context in the ffmpeg log — parse the `[Parsed_metadata_<N> @ 0x...]` prefix and group YAVG lines by N (the lower-indexed filter is [lm], the higher is [rm]); or, more robustly, give each chain a deterministic key via `metadata=print:file=<path>` (one file per ROI) or distinct `print:key=...left/right` and split by key. Add a serial smoke that runs the real two-ROI motionArgs against a fixture with motion on one side and asserts left/right energy ends up on the correct side and time.

title: child-process-gone wired to killAll() aborts every in-flight job on any Electron child crash
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/sidecar-manager.ts:344-353`

**Problem:** installLifecycleHooks registers `app.on('child-process-gone', kill)` where kill = killAll(). So a transient GPU-process crash (common on macOS under memory pressure, exactly when a big export is running) would trip killAll() and SIGTERM→SIGKILL every running transcribe/export, emitting CANCELLED to the user mid-encode even though the app keeps running. The intent (orphan prevention on quit) is right for before-quit/will-quit, but child-process-gone is too broad a trigger for a full job massacre.

**Recommendation:** Drop child-process-gone from the killAll hooks, or scope it: inspect the GoneDetails (event details include the process type and reason) and only killAll when it indicates the main/utility host is going down, not for a recoverable GPU process exit. Keep before-quit/will-quit/SIGINT/SIGTERM as the kill triggers.

title: ffmpeg/whisper/ffprobe argv built from user-controlled paths that may begin with '-' (flag injection)
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/ffmpeg-export.ts:222-252, src/main/services/whisper-spawn.ts:56-72, src/main/utils/ffprobe.ts:80-87`

**Problem:** sourcePath/outputPath (export), wavPath/model (whisper), and filePath (ffprobe) flow from renderer IPC/JobParams straight into spawn()/execFile() argv with no normalization. There is no shell, so classic shell injection is impossible, but ffmpeg/ffprobe/whisper-cli treat any argv token starting with '-' as an OPTION. exportClipArgs places outputPath as the final positional arg; an outputPath like '-y' or '-f' (or a sourcePath like '-protocol_whitelist...') would be parsed as a flag rather than a filename, letting a crafted path alter the encode (e.g. force a different muxer/protocol, write a sentinel file, or set arbitrary ffmpeg options). The export outputPath does come from a save dialog in the normal flow, but JOB_START('export', params) is callable directly by the renderer with an attacker-chosen outputPath, and sourcePath is taken verbatim from the project. None of the arg builders prefix '--' or validate the leading character.

**Recommendation:** At the spawn boundary, guard every path argument: reject (or refuse to spawn) any path beginning with '-', and where a tool supports it, terminate options with a literal '--' before positional file args (ffmpeg/ffprobe accept '--' is not universal — prefer prefixing relative paths with './' and rejecting leading-dash absolute basenames). Add a shared assertSafePathArg(path) helper used by ffmpeg-core/whisper-spawn/ffprobe.

title: .ocproj forward-compat claim is false: z.object strips unknown keys → silent data loss on load/re-save
description:
**Location:** `src/shared/schema.ts:20,291 + src/main/services/project-store.ts:118-147`

**Problem:** schema.ts:20 states persistence schemas use plain z.object that is "forward-compatible: tolerate unknown keys from newer versions," and project-store.ts:142 reports validation failure as "tampered or unsupported version." Both are inaccurate. I verified with Zod 4 that z.object STRIPS unknown keys rather than preserving them, and never fails on them. So when an OLDER app build (smaller schema) opens an .ocproj written by a NEWER build, loadProject succeeds but silently DROPS every newer field; the next autosave (saveProject, JSON.stringify of the parsed object) persists the stripped document — permanent data loss with no warning. There is also no schemaVersion/version field anywhere on Project, so there is no way to detect or gate cross-version loads.

**Recommendation:** Decide and implement the real policy: (a) if forward-compat-with-preservation is intended, use z.looseObject / .passthrough() on the persistence schemas (NOT the AI strictObject ones) so unknown future keys survive the round-trip; and/or (b) add an explicit schemaVersion: number to Project, stamp it on save, and on load branch on it (migrate-up or refuse-with-typed-error for versions newer than the app understands). At minimum, correct the misleading comments so the behavior is not assumed to be safe.

title: Export jobs never register a PID, so kill-on-quit/cancel has no OS-level SIGKILL backstop
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/jobs/export-runner.ts:107-202`

Cancellation/quit therefore relies ENTIRELY on the cooperative AbortSignal reaching ffmpeg-core's onAbort (SIGKILL). The PRD §17 design intentionally has a SIGTERM→SIGKILL escalation as the backstop for exactly the case where the cooperative path doesn't fire (e.g. an ffmpeg child wedged in a syscall, or the abort listener not yet attached because abort raced spawn). For the heaviest, longest-running job kind (a full re-encode), that backstop is silently absent.

**Recommendation:** Thread an onPid callback from the export runner through exportClip/detectSilences/planReframe into ffmpeg-core.runFfmpeg (mirroring whisper-spawn's onSpawn and url-download's onPid), and call ctx.trackPid(pid) for each spawned ffmpeg child so escalateKill can SIGKILL a wedged encoder on quit/cancel.

title: ffprobe duration 'N/A' becomes NaN and silently propagates into SourceVideo / timeline / progress
description:
**Location:** `src/main/utils/ffprobe.ts:68`

**Problem:** parseFfprobeJson computes duration: Number(json.format?.duration ?? 0). ffprobe emits the literal string "N/A" for format.duration on some real containers (fragmented MP4 without a top-level duration, certain MKV/transport streams, live captures). Number("N/A") is NaN, so SourceVideo.duration becomes NaN. The IMPORT_VIDEO handler (src/main/ipc/video.ts:177) returns this raw — the probe result is NOT re-validated through Zod at the IPC boundary — so NaN reaches the renderer untyped. Zod v4 (4.4.3 here) actually rejects NaN for z.number(), which means the failure surfaces LATER and confusingly: only when the project is persisted/loaded through Project.parse. Meanwhile downstream math breaks now: in audio.ts:30 the try/catch only catches throws, not a NaN result, so NaN flows into extractAudio as the progress denominator; progressPct's guard `totalDurationSec <= 0` is false for NaN, yielding NaN percentages; PreviewPlayer.tsx:55 uses { start:0, end: sourceVideo.duration } → NaN timeline bounds.

**Recommendation:** In parseFfprobeJson coerce defensively: const d = Number(json.format?.duration); duration = Number.isFinite(d) && d > 0 ? d : 0 (or fall back to the longest stream's duration tag). Returning a finite 0 keeps it Zod-valid and lets the UI show 'unknown duration' instead of NaN-poisoning the timeline. Separately consider validating the probe result through SourceVideo.parse() at the IPC boundary so a bad probe fails fast as INPUT_INVALID rather than at save time.

title: Clamp-before-dedupe discards the higher-scoring of two overlapping cross-chunk duplicates
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/ai-client.ts:444-450`

**Problem:** In mapReduceGenerate the order is reconcile -> clampDetectedClips -> dedupeAndRank. clampDetectedClips (line 279-285) drops overlapping spans keeping the EARLIER-STARTING one, while dedupeAndRank (line 382-390) is documented to keep the HIGHER-SCORING one. Because clamp runs first, when the same viral moment is returned by two adjacent chunks (the overlap region re-sends it, so this is the COMMON case, not an edge case) with slightly different bounds, clamp keeps whichever started earlier and throws away the other before dedupeAndRank can compare scores. title: Renderer parks a permanent waiter + main runs a consumer-less job if JOB_PORT transfer is skipped
description:
**Location:** `src/main/index.ts:214-219; src/renderer/src/hooks/jobPort.ts:66-76`

**Problem:** wireJobControlPlane starts the job (line 214, returns jobId) BEFORE transferring port2, then only transfers it `if (frame)` (line 217-218). If event.senderFrame is null (frame navigated/destroyed between invoke and handler) the JOB_PORT message is never sent, yet startJob already enqueued the work and returned a jobId. The renderer's runExport/runModelDownload then await acquireJobPort(jobId) which parks a waiter in the `waiters` map that is NEVER resolved (jobPort.ts:73-75) — the start promise hangs forever and the for-await loop never runs. Meanwhile the main-side job runs to completion (or error), posting all events into port1 whose peer port2 was never delivered, so the buffered events are never drained and the port is closed only at settle. There is no timeout or rejection fallback on either side.

**Recommendation:** If `!frame`, immediately cancel the just-started job (sidecar.cancel(jobId)) before returning, OR move the postMessage to occur before startJob and bail if the frame is gone. On the renderer side, give acquireJobPort an optional timeout that rejects the waiter (and deletes it from the map) so a never-arriving port surfaces as a typed error instead of an eternal hang.

title: acquireJobPort() waits forever with no timeout — any dropped port hangs the whole job consumer
description:
**Location:** `src/renderer/src/hooks/jobPort.ts:66-76`

**Problem:** acquireJobPort(jobId) returns a Promise that is only ever resolved when a matching JOB_PORT message arrives; if the port is never delivered there is NO timeout and NO rejection. The port can legitimately fail to arrive: in main/index.ts:217-218 the JOB_PORT post is guarded `if (frame) frame.postMessage(...)`, so when `event.senderFrame` is null (frame destroyed/navigated during the invoke) the renderer already has its `{jobId}` (jobs.start resolved) but port2 is silently dropped. Every consumer — runImportPipeline (import-pipeline.ts:65), runExport (export-run.ts:39), runModelDownload (model-download.ts:59), runUrlDownload (import-pipeline.ts:114) — then `await acquireJobPort(jobId)` and hangs forever. The import controller stays busy:true with error:null, batch-export's Promise.all never settles, and the user sees a permanently-stuck progress bar. This directly violates the spirit of the 'never a silent hang' invariant: the event-stream invariant holds, but nothing guarantees the renderer ever GETS the stream.

**Recommendation:** Give acquireJobPort a bounded wait: reject (or resolve to a sentinel that the consumers map to an error) after a timeout (e.g. 30s — the port is delivered on the same tick as the invoke response, so any real delay means it's gone), clearing the waiter from `waiters`. Belt-and-suspenders: in main/index.ts treat a null senderFrame as a hard failure — synchronously settle the just-started job with an error via the manager (or cancel it) so the stream terminates instead of dangling.

title: Reframe detector buffers all raw RGB frames in memory before inference (~220 MB/clip)
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/reframe-detect.ts:396-410`

**Problem:** detectReframe pipes raw rawvideo from ffmpeg to stdout and `defaultRunFfmpegCaptureStdout` accumulates every chunk into `out: Buffer[]` then `Buffer.concat(out)` (line 496), so the ENTIRE decoded frame stream is resident before a single YuNet inference runs. At the default 2 fps and 640x640x3 bytes/frame, a 90s max-duration clip = 180 frames × 1.23 MB ≈ 221 MB held at once, transiently doubled during Buffer.concat. With the sidecar export queue running up to min(2, ceil(cores/4)) exports concurrently (and batch-export fanning out all approved clips), two simultaneous reframe analyses can spike ~450 MB+ for nothing — the frames are consumed sequentially and could be processed as they arrive.

**Recommendation:** Stream-consume the rawvideo: read fixed 640*640*3-byte frames off ffmpeg stdout as they arrive (slice complete frames from a rolling buffer), run YuNet on each and discard it, keeping only the small FaceBox[] per sample. This caps memory at ~1 frame regardless of clip length and overlaps decode with inference. Alternatively lower the default sampleFps or scale frames smaller, but streaming is the real fix.

title: acquireJobPort can hang forever — no timeout/reject, leaks parked waiter if port never arrives
description:
**Location:** `src/renderer/src/hooks/jobPort.ts:66-76`

**Problem:** acquireJobPort parks a waiter resolver in the `waiters` map and returns a Promise that ONLY ever resolves when a JOB_PORT message arrives — it never rejects and has no timeout. In main/index.ts:217-218 the port is posted via `event.senderFrame.postMessage(JOB_PORT, ...)` guarded by `if (frame)`: if senderFrame is null (frame navigated/destroyed in the window between JOB_START returning {jobId} and the post), the port is never sent, yet JOB_START still resolves {jobId}. The renderer then awaits acquireJobPort forever and the consumer (runImportPipeline/runExport/runModelDownload) hangs with no error and no progress — silently breaking the 'every job terminates, never a silent hang' invariant from the renderer's side. The parked resolver also leaks in the waiters map. Additionally, two acquireJobPort(id) calls for the same id would overwrite the first waiter (first promise never resolves), though in practice each jobId is acquired once.

**Recommendation:** Give acquireJobPort an optional AbortSignal/timeout that rejects the parked waiter (and deletes it from the map) so callers fail loudly instead of hanging. Have callers pass a generous timeout. Optionally, in main/index.ts, if senderFrame is falsy, cancel the just-started job and signal an error rather than leaving the renderer waiting.

title: Motion ROIs (2.8x face-width tiles) overlap when speakers are only ~15% of width apart, so each side's motion energy contains the other speaker
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/reframe-detect.ts:651-666 (ROIs from clusterTileRegion) + src/shared/reframe-plan.ts:101,108-109,342-352`

**Problem:** clusterTwoFaceRegions only requires the two clusters' centers to be >= 15% of frame width apart (MIN_CLUSTER_GAP_FRAC, e.g. 288px on a 1920-wide source). But the per-side motion ROI is clusterTileRegion's tile, sized ~2.8*faceW wide (e.g. a 200px face -> 560px tile). Two tiles whose centers are only 288px apart but each 560px wide overlap by ~270px. The overlapping band feeds BOTH the left and right tblend+signalstats chains, so when speaker A talks, speaker A's mouth motion also raises speaker B's energy. ACTIVE_MARGIN (1.15x) discrimination degrades exactly in the close-speaker case the feature most needs to handle, biasing toward whichever side the overlap favors.

**Recommendation:** Derive the motion ROIs from a non-overlapping partition (e.g. split the frame at the midpoint between the two cluster centers, or clip each tile so left.x+left.w <= right.x), rather than reusing the visually-oversized split tiles. Keep the wide tiles only for the split-screen render; use tight, mutually-exclusive ROIs for the motion-energy comparison.

The final check is `if (expected && actual !== expected)`, so when `expected` is undefined the verification is SKIPPED ENTIRELY and the downloaded bytes are kept. KNOWN_SHA256 only pins `tiny`; for base/small/medium/turbo/large-v3 verification depends solely on HF returning the `x-linked-etag` header. If HF (or a CDN/proxy/mirror) omits that header — a header-only, not byte-level, signal — a corrupt or tampered multi-GB model is written to userData/models and used for transcription. This directly contradicts the module header's stated guarantee: 'refusing to keep a file whose hash we cannot confirm OR that mismatches (no corrupt model on disk).' No test covers the no-etag/no-known-hash path (tests/unit/model-manager.spec.ts only covers explicit-sha, etag-present, and mismatch).

**Recommendation:** Treat a missing `expected` as a hard failure for any model not in KNOWN_SHA256: if `!expected`, cleanup() and throw an 'unable to verify model integrity' error rather than returning success. Better, pin KNOWN_SHA256 for all six sizes (the values are public and stable) so verification never depends on a response header. At minimum, log a loud warning and surface it to the user when a model is accepted without hash confirmation.

title: Cancelling a queued (not-yet-admitted) job doesn't emit terminal CANCELLED until the limiter admits it
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/sidecar-manager.ts:288-296,314-319`

**Problem:** When a job is queued behind a serialized kind (transcribe concurrency = 1), startJob has scheduled `limiter.add(async () => { if (aborted) emit.error('CANCELLED'…); … })`. cancel(jobId) aborts the controller and runs escalateKill (no PIDs → no-op) but does NOT emit any terminal event itself — the CANCELLED error is only produced when the limiter eventually ADMITS the task. So if the user cancels a queued transcribe while the in-flight one is still running, the renderer (which awaits the CANCELLED JobEvent to tear down its UI/port) gets no terminal event until the head-of-line job finishes. If that head job hangs, the cancelled-queued job never terminates and lingers in `active` — a silent-hang corner for the queued job, which is exactly what the §10.2 invariant forbids.

**Recommendation:** In cancel(), if the job hasn't started running yet (track a `started` flag set when the limiter admits the task), settle it immediately with {t:'error',code:'CANCELLED'} and delete it from active, rather than waiting for the limiter to admit-then-reject. The Limiter has no remove(), so a started-flag short-circuit in the settle path is the cleanest fix.

title: model-download cancel does not release the fetch ReadableStream reader (socket/stream leak)
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/model-manager.ts:164-213`

**Problem:** On abort, onAbort (line 166-169) calls out.destroy() and rejects, and the pump loop (line 185-192) throws on the next iteration when it sees signal.aborted. But the fetch response reader obtained at line 175 (`res.body.getReader()`) is never `reader.cancel()`'d or `releaseLock()`'d on the abort/error path. Because `fetchImpl(url, { signal })` is passed the same signal, the global fetch will abort the underlying request in most runtimes — but the explicit reader holds a lock and an in-flight read() promise that is never settled or cancelled, and the manual sink Writable is also never destroyed. For a 2.9GB large-v3 download cancelled mid-stream this can leave the body reader/socket pinned until GC. Additionally, every chunk is written twice through two layers (sink.write at pump line 190 AND out.write inside the sink's write() at line 181) which is correct but fragile; the abort path destroys `out` but not `sink`.

**Recommendation:** In onAbort and the .catch handler, call `reader.cancel().catch(()=>{})` (or `reader.releaseLock()`) and `sink.destroy()` in addition to out.destroy(), so the body stream is torn down deterministically rather than relying on the fetch signal alone.

title: source-media URL comment claims pathToFileURL parity but uses encodeURIComponent
description:
**Location:** `src/renderer/src/components/source-media.ts:28-40`

**Problem:** The doc comment says the encoding 'Uses encodeURI semantics per segment via the WHATWG URL builder so the percent-encoding matches Node's pathToFileURL' and 'guarantees byte-for-byte agreement.' The code actually does plain encodeURIComponent per '/'-split segment — which encodes MORE than pathToFileURL (e.g. + → %2B, & → %26, ( ) ! ' left unescaped). The round trip is in fact correct because BOTH processes use the same encodeURIComponent/decodeURIComponent pair (I verified apostrophes, parens, +, &, #, %, all round-trip), so the actual decoder is pathFromMediaUrl (not fileURLToPath). The comment is just wrong about the mechanism, which is a trap for the next maintainer who might 'fix' one side to real pathToFileURL semantics and silently break the byte-equality the source-media.spec round-trip test depends on.

**Recommendation:** Correct the comment to state plainly: both sides percent-encode each '/'-separated segment with encodeURIComponent and decode with decodeURIComponent; the contract is the encodeURIComponent/decodeURIComponent symmetry (asserted by source-media.spec), NOT pathToFileURL parity. Note that pathToFileURL is only used later by the main handler to feed net.fetch, after pathFromMediaUrl has already decoded.

title: Permanent download failures are surfaced as retriable SIDECAR_CRASH
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/sidecar-manager.ts:302-303; src/main/services/url-download.ts:163-166; src/main/services/model-manager.ts:217-222`

**Problem:** Any non-cancel throw from a runner is mapped to emit.error('SIDECAR_CRASH', message, true) — retriable:true. title: Production CSP connect-src allows any https origin, widening exfiltration if the renderer is compromised
description:
**Location:** `src/main/index.ts:92-100`

**Problem:** The prod CSP uses connect-src 'self' https: — necessary because BYOK calls go to OpenAI/Anthropic/OpenRouter/etc. and the user can set a custom baseUrl. But combined with the arbitrary-file-read primitive in the media protocol (finding #1), 'connect-src https:' means a compromised renderer can POST exfiltrated file bytes to ANY https endpoint, not just the configured provider. Note the AI provider calls themselves originate in the MAIN process (ai-client.ts fetch), NOT the renderer, so the renderer does not actually need broad https connect access for normal operation — the OpenRouter model-list fetch is also main-side. The wide grant is therefore larger than the renderer's legitimate need.

**Recommendation:** Since provider network calls happen in main (not the renderer), tighten the renderer connect-src to 'self' (plus the media scheme/blob for media) and drop 'https:' — or, if any renderer-side fetch is truly required, restrict to the specific provider hosts. This sharply limits the blast radius of any renderer compromise. Verify no renderer code does a direct cross-origin fetch before tightening.

title: Cancelled audio extraction poisons the content-addressed WAV cache
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/ffmpeg-extract.ts:85-107`

**Problem:** extractAudio writes the WAV directly to its final cache path `wavPath` with ffmpeg `-y` (audioExtractArgs). The cache key (wavCacheKey) is derived from the SOURCE file's size+mtime, not the WAV's completeness. On cancel/quit the ffmpeg child is SIGKILLed (ffmpeg-core onAbort), leaving a truncated WAV at wavPath. There is no try/finally to remove the partial file on abort. The very next extract for the same source hits `if (existsSync(wavPath))` at line 92 and returns the partial/corrupt WAV as a cache hit (cached:true), which whisper then either fails on or transcribes incompletely — with no signal that the cache is poisoned. Unlike model-manager.downloadModel (which rm()s the partial on abort) and url-download (which discards its tmp), this path has no cleanup.

**Recommendation:** Extract to a temp filename (e.g. `<wavPath>.partial`) and atomically rename to wavPath only after runFfmpeg resolves successfully; on reject/abort rm the partial. This makes the presence of wavPath a true 'complete' signal and prevents serving a killed extraction as a cache hit.

description:

description:

title: ffmpeg progress parsing has no line buffer — split chunks drop progress samples
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/ffmpeg-core.ts:133-143`

**Problem:** child.stderr 'data' handler calls parseFfmpegProgress(text) on each raw chunk independently with no carry-over buffer for an incomplete trailing line. FFmpeg's -progress writes key=value lines, but a chunk boundary can split a line mid-token (e.g. 'out_time_us=12' then '34567\n', or 'out_ti'+'me_us=...'). parseFfmpegProgress only honors fully-seen key=value pairs, so the split line is mis-parsed (wrong key → ignored) and that progress sample is lost. This is cosmetic (progress bar stutters/skips, no incorrect completion since progress=end arrives on its own line and out_time is monotonic), but it undermines the smoothness the helper exists to provide.

**Recommendation:** Carry a residual buffer in the closure: accumulate `buf += text`, split on the last newline, parse the complete prefix, and keep the trailing partial line for the next chunk. parseFfmpegProgress stays pure; only runFfmpeg's data handler needs the buffer. Mirror this in whisper-spawn.ts which has the same per-chunk pattern for progress.

description:

**Recommendation:** Once the series are disambiguated by filter instance (see the related finding), pair by matching pts_time per side rather than by index, and if the per-side counts differ, truncate to the common timestamps (or bail to static-on-dominant). title: Fallback array limiter permanently starves a kind if a task body throws synchronously
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/sidecar-manager.ts:361-390`

**Problem:** defaultArrayLimiterFactory's run() (line 377-383) calls `task().then(resolve,reject).finally(()=>{activeCount-=1; pump()})`. If `task()` throws SYNCHRONOUSLY (rather than returning a rejected promise), the exception propagates out of run() before .then/.finally are attached, so activeCount is never decremented and pump() is never re-invoked — that kind's slot is permanently consumed, starving all subsequent jobs of that kind. In production the p-queue factory is used (set in main/index.ts:241), but this array limiter is the documented fallback when p-queue fails to load (main/index.ts:242-244) and is the default in tests. The task passed by startJob (line 289-296) is an async fn so it normally returns a rejected promise, but any synchronous throw before the first await (e.g. a runner that throws on argument validation synchronously) would trigger this.

**Recommendation:** Wrap the task invocation so a synchronous throw is converted to a rejected promise: `Promise.resolve().then(task).then(resolve,reject).finally(...)`, guaranteeing the finally (and thus pump()/activeCount decrement) always runs.

title: chunkSegments does not isolate an oversized segment and re-carries it into every later chunk (O(n^2) token cost)
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/ai-client.ts:313-339`

**Problem:** The doc comment (line 310-311) claims 'A single oversized segment forms its own chunk (never split mid-segment)', but the code never isolates it. Because each new chunk is seeded with current = the time-overlap of the prior chunk, an oversized segment (one whose tokens exceed maxTokens) that ends near a chunk boundary always satisfies the time-overlap filter `s.end > boundaryEnd - overlapSeconds` and is re-included in the next chunk, and the next, until it ages out of the overlap window. Verified by simulation: a single 20000-token segment lands in a chunk with the prior segment (20011 tokens) and is then re-sent in the following chunk too. For long monologue segments this multiplies token spend (and cost/latency) and can blow past model context limits. Separately, the overlap filter selects by TIME but chunks are split by TOKENS, so a long overlapSeconds relative to chunk duration re-includes the entire previous chunk (each chunk then adds only one new segment) — also verified.

**Recommendation:** When a single segment's estimated tokens alone exceed maxTokens, flush the current chunk and emit that segment as its own chunk with no overlap carry-over, then reset current=[]. Also cap the overlap so it can never re-include the whole prior chunk (e.g. limit overlap segments by count or by a fraction of the chunk).

title: Karaoke \k durations rounded independently can drift from the Dialogue End
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/ass-captions.ts:205`

**Problem:** Each gap syllable and each word duration is rounded to centiseconds independently (toCentiseconds(w.start - prevEnd) and toCentiseconds(w.end - w.start)), and the Dialogue Start/End are separately rounded from startSec/endSec. The accumulated sum of \k values for a line is not guaranteed to equal (End - Start) in centiseconds; over a multi-word line the karaoke fill can finish a few cs before or after the line's End. It is sub-frame and cosmetic, but it means the last word's highlight can complete slightly out of step with the spoken audio on longer lines.

**Recommendation:** Accept it as cosmetic, or eliminate drift by computing each cue boundary as the difference of cumulative rounded offsets (round absolute boundaries to cs first, then take consecutive differences) so the \k sum is exactly End-Start.

title: Anthropic transport hardcodes max_tokens:4096, can truncate large clip outputs into a wasted repair round-trip
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/ai-client.ts:534-540`

**Problem:** buildAnthropicTransport sends a fixed max_tokens:4096 on every messages.parse call. The ClipSchema output is large per clip (title, hook, suggested_caption, hashtags[], keywords[], the 6-field virality object, plus analysis). With a higher numClips the JSON can exceed 4096 output tokens, in which case Anthropic truncates the response mid-JSON → safeParse fails → the one repair round-trip is consumed re-emitting an equally-truncated response → INPUT_INVALID. title: Static-vs-pan deadzone and static crop center are computed from the EMA-lagged path, biasing the decision and the resting position toward early samples
description:
**Location:** `src/shared/reframe-plan.ts:651-668`

**Problem:** The single-speaker path smooths centers with EMA alpha=0.2 seeded at xs[0] (emaSmooth :539-543), then decides static vs pan from max(smoothed)-min(smoothed) <= deadzonePx and, when static, centers the crop on mean(smoothed). Because a 0.2 EMA seeded at the first sample lags heavily and never reaches the true extremes, (a) a face that genuinely sweeps but slowly can have a compressed smoothed range that stays under the ~1.5% deadzone and wrongly render as static, and (b) the static cropX is pulled toward the early-sample position rather than the true central tendency (mean of raw centers / median). For a clip that starts with the speaker off-center this resting crop is visibly off.

**Recommendation:** Make the static/pan threshold from the raw (or lightly-smoothed) center range, and center the static crop on the median or plain mean of the raw weighted centers rather than mean(smoothed). Keep EMA only for the pan keyframe path where temporal smoothing is the goal. Add a test asserting a slow full-width sweep is classified as pan, not static.

title: transcriptHash is a 32-bit FNV-1a — collision-prone for a process-global cache key
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/ai-client.ts:342-350`

**Problem:** transcriptHash folds the entire segment stream (start|end|text per segment) into a single 32-bit FNV-1a value rendered as hex. The clipCache (ipc/ai.ts:121) is a process-global Map keyed in part by this hash. 32-bit space gives a non-trivial birthday-collision probability across many distinct transcripts in a long-running session; a collision returns one project's clip results for a different project/transcript. Low likelihood in practice (cache is in-memory and per-session) but the consequence (cross-project wrong clips) is silent and confusing.

**Recommendation:** Use a wider/standard digest for the cache key — e.g. Node's crypto.createHash('sha1'/'sha256') over the same serialized string (this is main-process Node code, so crypto is available). Cheap and removes the collision concern entirely.

title: secrets.json written world-readable with no restrictive file mode
description:
**Location:** `src/main/utils/security.ts:54-58`

**Problem:** fileBackend.write persists the encrypted-key map to userData/secrets.json via writeFileSync without a mode, so it inherits the process umask (typically 0644 — readable by any local user/process). The key value itself is safeStorage-encrypted (good defense-in-depth), but on macOS the safeStorage key is derived from the app's keychain entry; a co-resident local attacker who can read the file plus prompt/replay the keychain (or on Linux where safeStorage may fall back to a weaker basic_text backend) gains more than necessary. There is no reason for this BYOK secrets file to be group/other readable.

**Recommendation:** Write secrets.json with mode 0o600 (writeFileSync(path, data, { mode: 0o600 }) and chmod existing files on first write), matching the least-privilege intent of the safeStorage gate. Cheap defense-in-depth.

title: killAll deletes jobs from `active` but leaves the queued limiter task to fire emit.error on a port that was already closed elsewhere
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/sidecar-manager.ts:331-337,243-253`

**Problem:** killAll() aborts each controller and immediately `this.active.delete(jobId)`, but a queued job's task still sits inside the limiter. When the limiter later admits it, the closure calls emit.error('CANCELLED', …) → settle(), which calls port.postMessage + port.close on a port whose peer was already torn down at quit. Combined with the empty-pids escalateKill, killAll on an all-queued workload effectively does nothing until the event loop drains.

**Recommendation:** Have killAll (and cancel) settle queued jobs synchronously via the same started-flag short-circuit suggested for the cancel finding, so the terminal CANCELLED is delivered and the job removed deterministically instead of depending on the limiter draining.

title: Tracked PIDs are never removed on normal child exit — escalateKill can SIGKILL a reused (foreign) PID
description:
**Location:** `src/main/services/sidecar-manager.ts:280,322-328`

**Problem:** trackPid only ever adds to job.pids (`job.pids.add(pid)`); there is no untrack on child close. For a multi-child job (url-download spawns yt-dlp AND then a separate faststart ffmpeg child — see url-download.ts:381 and faststartRemux at url-download.ts:300-307, each calling onPid→trackPid), the first child's PID stays in the set after it exits. When the job is later cancelled or the app quits, escalateKill sends SIGTERM and (after the 3s grace) SIGKILL to EVERY accumulated PID — including PIDs whose process already exited and may have been recycled by the OS to an unrelated process. The injected killPid swallows ESRCH, but a recycled PID is a live process, so this can kill an innocent bystander process.

**Recommendation:** Give JobRunnerContext an untrackPid(pid) (or have trackPid return a disposer) and call it from each spawn wrapper's close/error handler, so job.pids only ever holds currently-live children. At minimum, scope the SIGKILL sweep to PIDs added since the SIGTERM, or record spawn time and skip PIDs known to have exited.
